summary: Namibia keeps visa-free entry for SADC citizens and reciprocating states, but since April 1, 2025 it requires a visa from other nationalities — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada and Japan, which can get it on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals); nationalities not on the visa-on-arrival list must obtain an e-visa before travel.

tips.text: The UK government's travel advice says accidents are common on gravel and dirt roads and that many gravel roads deteriorate in the rainy season (January to April). For that season it advises not going faster than 80 km/h, carrying 2 spare tyres and avoiding driving at night outside towns, where wildlife and livestock are serious hazards.

Namibia's entry rules changed on April 1, 2025 — many nationalities that used to enter free (EU states, US, UK, Canada, Japan and others) now pay NAD 1,600 per adult for a visa on arrival or e-visa. Check your status shortly before travel, as the lists may still be adjusted.

The UK government's travel advice says Namibian immigration officials will not accept an abridged birth certificate: children aged 17 and under need a full one with both parents' details, plus an affidavit of consent from any parent or guardian who is not travelling.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Namibia?
faq.answer: It changed in 2025. SADC citizens and nationals of countries that waive visas for Namibians still enter visa-free. Since April 1, 2025, citizens of many previously-exempt countries — including most EU states, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Japan — must obtain a visa, available on arrival or online in advance for NAD 1,600 per adult (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals). Nationalities not on the visa-on-arrival list must get an e-visa before travelling.

faq.question: How does Namibia's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationals present their passport at Hosea Kutako or Walvis Bay airport or a main border post, pay NAD 1,600 per adult (NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals; NAD 800 or 600 for children aged 6–11, free under 6) by card, and receive a multiple-entry visa for up to 90 days. To skip lines you can apply in advance as an e-visa through the Ministry of Home Affairs eServices portal.

faq.question: Who can still enter Namibia visa-free?
faq.answer: Citizens of SADC countries (South Africa, Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Angola and the rest) and of states that reciprocate Namibia's waiver — for example Russia, Singapore and Malaysia — continue to enter without a visa, typically for up to 90 days. Confirm your status before travel as the lists are periodically reviewed.

faq.question: Do children need extra documents to enter Namibia?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government's travel advice says children aged 17 and under must carry a valid passport and a full (unabridged) birth certificate with both parents' details; if a child travels with one parent, the other should give consent in an affidavit. Canada's advice also requires a long-form birth certificate and proof of consent.

faq.question: What should I know before driving in Namibia?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says road conditions are generally good, but most roads outside urban areas are gravel, and fatal accidents — often linked to excessive speed on gravel — are common, many involving a single tourist vehicle. It advises avoiding night-time driving outside urban centres and notes that roadside assistance is unreliable or non-existent outside Windhoek.
